headline: Biological foundation models face scrutiny over pretraining, benchmarks, and baselines
label: Biological Foundation Model Evaluation
summary: Recent preprints re-examine whether DNA, single-cell, and perturbation models outperform simple baselines under standardized evaluation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the evaluation of large learned models on biological sequences and profiles, with attention to what pretraining objectives, data, and baselines actually contribute. A DNA language model study identifies flaws in pretraining, including downstream datasets, neighbor-masking, and vocabulary, and introduces a standardized testbed for reproducible comparison. A systematic evaluation of 11 genomic language models on regulatory genomics tasks finds limited gains over random baselines, attributed to sequence-only self-supervised pretraining. In single-cell RNA-seq, benchmarking of five foundation models on more than 1.5 million cells finds scVI ranks top against Harmony. A perturbation-prediction study proposes Signal, Bounds, and Baselines principles, noting that deep models, including foundation models, often fail. Generative work includes SAVE, a conditional flow-matching Transformer for multi-condition single-cell generation, and AROMA, a multimodal reasoning model for virtual-cell perturbation prediction. The new element is methodological: rigorous benchmarks and baselines are the focus.
